transcript.sitrep:
SITUATION (Week 1). A novel respiratory virus has been confirmed in three US cities, with likely undetected spread. Early case reports are alarming but the sample is tiny and biased toward the sickest. You do not yet know the true infection-fatality rate or how transmissible it is. Hospitals in the affected cities report rising admissions. Markets fell 4% on the news. The WHO has called an emergency meeting.

Your health agencies want aggressive early action 'to be safe'; your economic team warns that shutting down on a maybe could be its own catastrophe; governors are looking to you for a lead but guard their authority. Every option has a cost, and you must choose before the data is in. What do you do?

actions.name: surge_testing

params.rationale: We are flying blind on true severity and transmissibility; we need immediate, widespread testing and genomic sequencing to guide decisions before committing to a full shutdown.

actions.rationale: We are flying blind on true severity and transmissibility; we need immediate, widespread testing and genomic sequencing to guide decisions before committing to a full shutdown.

actions.name: invoke_dpa

params.rationale: Starting production now for tests, PPE, and ventilators is cheap insurance; if this gets worse, global supply chains will collapse and we will be too late.

actions.rationale: Starting production now for tests, PPE, and ventilators is cheap insurance; if this gets worse, global supply chains will collapse and we will be too late.

actions.name: candid_briefings

params.rationale: Honesty about what we know and do not know builds public trust, encourages voluntary precautions, and prevents panic far better than reassuring spin.

actions.rationale: Honesty about what we know and do not know builds public trust, encourages voluntary precautions, and prevents panic far better than reassuring spin.

params.rationale: A single transparent federal data hub reduces confusion, lets states and hospitals plan, and holds all levels of government accountable.

actions.rationale: A single transparent federal data hub reduces confusion, lets states and hospitals plan, and holds all levels of government accountable.
